gary_2026_08_14_the_ai_briefing_by_start.title: The AI Briefing By Startup Grind - Agentic Governance
gary_2026_08_14_the_ai_briefing_by_start.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_08_14_the_ai_briefing_by_start.summary: Gary's Guide: The AI Briefing is a high-velocity roundtable for decision-makers brought to you by Startup Grind. We bypass the hype by dissecting one high-signal industry deck with a room of vetted founders, operators, & enterprise executives. No lectures-just a 60-minute deep-dive into the tactics & data defining your next quarter. The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise. This Month's Source: The AI Agent Governance Gap: What CISOs Need Now (Cloud Security Alliance AI Safety Initiative - Apr 2026) Gartner projects that 40% of enterprise applications will embed task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, up from less than 5% in 2025. However, it's becoming clear that governance hasn't kept pace with that curve. A 2026 survey of CISOs & CIOs at large enterprises found that 92% of them lack full visibility into their own AI agent identities. 95% doubt they could detect or contain a compromised agent if one turned up. That leaves a real gap for enterprises deploying agents today. No enforceable standard exists yet, & the frameworks most organizations already lean on (NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, the EU AI Act) were built for AI that responds to a prompt, not for AI that plans & takes action across outside systems on its own. The Mission: Who owns the agent when it acts? This session is co-hosted with Lazy 8 AI, an engineering collective focused on the transition from manual coding to managing autonomous AI systems. We'll use the report's own gaps, especially around identity & incident response, as the anchor for a broader conversation: what readiness actually looks like when the standards bodies are still a year or more behind the deployments. The Format: We'll open with the numbers: 92% of CISOs & CIOs blind to their own agent identities, & a standards timeline that leaves them on their own well into 2026. The room debates the report's own recommendations: agent inventories, least-privilege credentials, agent-specific incident response. What's realistic for a team that's already stretched, & what's closer to theater. Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Understand the exposure your organization is carrying right now, before a standard exists to measure against, & what following best practice will need to mean when a regulator or a board comes knocking. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on what you're actually doing today to track agent identity, permissions, & incident response, & where the gap between what leadership assumes & what's built is widest. Founders & Builders: See where the governance tooling gap is actually a product opportunity, & why the report's own commercial incentives should make you skeptical of framework adoption as the automatic answer. The Prep: This is a working session. Review the report here. Bring your perspective.

Details: Date: Aug 19, 2026 Time: 6:00pm - 8:30pm Venue: Private Dinner Club in NYC Past attendees of my events include the founders/C-suite of Venmo, Duolingo, Foursquare, Lyft, Goldman Sachs, Compass, Superhuman, Yext, OpenDoor, Chief, LearnVest, DocSend, Vercel, Loom, Morning Brew, The Hustle, Gas, Teachable, Replit, Twitter, Slack, Pinterest, Yahoo, MongoDB, Business Insider, Wonder, Hinge. Andrew has hosted over 300 events for 50,000 founders, operators, investors, & tech professionals that were featured by Bloomberg, Business Insider, Fast Company, Fortune Magazine, Axios, Newsweek, & Forbes. Business Insider dubbed him the "Gatsby of Silicon Alley." Hubble is NYC's largest online platform for startup office space. gary_2026_08_19_fundraising_launchpad_ea.title: Fundraising Launchpad - Early-Stage AI Startups
gary_2026_08_19_fundraising_launchpad_ea.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_08_19_fundraising_launchpad_ea.summary: Gary's Guide: Are you building an AI startup & preparing to raise capital? The Fundraising Launchpad helps early-stage AI founders in New York City prepare for fundraising by evaluating the strength of their technology & connecting the most promising startups with investors. Through the techtrust.ai Technology Trust framework, your startup receives a (confidential) Technology Trust Score that highlights the credibility, defensibility, & maturity of your AI technology. Selected startups are invited to a 15-minute pitch & evaluation session with the techtrust.ai team, designed to help you sharpen your fundraising story. Top startups are then introduced directly to our VC & angel partners as part of curated AI deal flow. How it works 1.Apply Apply your AI startup for the event via our form: https://tinyurl.com/ytmnu6dj 2.Technology Trust Score Your startup receives a confidential Technology Trust Score. 3.Founder Session Selected startups join the 15-minute pitch & evaluation session on Aug 19 at 6PM with the techtrust.ai team in NYC. 4.Investor Introductions Top startups are forwarded & introduced to our VC & angel partners. Spots are limited.

gary_2026_08_20_the_startup_pitch_demo_s.summary: Gary's Guide: See the newest companies coming out of the NYC startup ecosystem. Provide peer feedback & network with ambitious founders at The Startup Pitch: Demo Showcase. It's time to go beyond the deck & see the best live tech from New York's emerging startups. jc_culture_39177_2026_08_15_west_indian_.summary: County Commissioner Bill O’Dea and Chico Ramchal along side the West Indian American Committee will be holding a West Indian Family Fun Day at Lincoln Park, on August 15th, 2026 beginning at 11am and concluding at 8:00pm. This event is intended to provide a day and location where families of a West Indian background of Hudson County can congregate and celebrate their culture. It will also provide an insight to experience the West Indian culture if you are from any descent. Among culture sharing the committee will provide a host of community games for all age groups. Some of these activities include a tug-o-war, 100m race, sack race, etc. In conjunction with the activities, we will have a show mobile on location that will provide music and non-band performances, such as cultural dancing. The expected turnout is estimated at, with the committee providing over 50 volunteers to help support the event.

jc_culture_42565_2026_08_19_true_colors_.title: True Colors, Carried On: A Pride Gathering on Grief and Legacy
jc_culture_42565_2026_08_19_true_colors_.label: Art / Culture
jc_culture_42565_2026_08_19_true_colors_.place: Pet Shop, 193 Newark Ave, Jersey City, NJ
jc_culture_42565_2026_08_19_true_colors_.summary: This Pride, what if our true colors included the ones we’ve lost? True Colors, Carried On is an evening of small-group, facilitated conversation about dying, grief, and the legacies we leave behind, held in Jersey City during Pride Month. This isn’t therapy, it’s community and permission to say the word “death” out loud during a month that’s usually about celebration, because both things can be true at once. Consider bringing a photo or small keepsake of someone you’re carrying. If you don’t have one on hand, we’ll have materials for you to write out a memory or decorate a name tag when you arrive.

jc_culture_10003566_2026_09_02_hamilton_.summary: Join us at the Hamilton Park Farmers Market, your midweek destination for fresh, local, and thoughtfully crafted food and goods. Each week, we’re proud to feature farm-fresh produce from Stony Hill Farm alongside a curated selection of specialty vendors. Browse a variety of offerings including our long time vendor Pickles and Olives, fresh seafood from Scale Fish Market, and prepared foods perfect for dinner. You can also find baked goods, candles, personal care products, and more. You can even take advantage of convenient services like on-site knife sharpening while you shop. On the first and second Wednesdays of each month, enjoy live entertainment that adds to the vibrant, community atmosphere of the market. Whether you’re shopping for the week, grabbing a bite, or simply enjoying the park, the Hamilton Park Farmers Market is a welcoming space to connect with local vendors and neighbors.
